overview: This enum chooses the world position used to place a hit effect when an attack connects.

None.simple: The hit effect appears at the reported contact point.
None.technical: FGameDataTableRow_Damage defaults HitEffectLocationType to None. BuildHitEffectSpawnParams has no explicit None case, so the default branch copies Request.Location into OutParams.Location.

ImpactPoint.simple: The hit effect appears at the reported contact point.
ImpactPoint.technical: Declared as ImpactPoint. BuildHitEffectSpawnParams has no explicit ImpactPoint case, so the default branch copies Request.Location into OutParams.Location.

Receiver.simple: The hit effect appears on the target waist.
Receiver.technical: The Receiver case asks the receiver mesh for the bone index of waist and uses that bone transform location. A missing mesh or an INDEX_NONE bone result falls back to Receiver GAISlot015_LocationLike.

HitComponent.simple: The hit effect appears at the struck body component.
HitComponent.technical: The HitComponent case calls Request.HitComponent.Get()->GetComponentLocation() and copies the result into OutParams.Location. The traced function performs no validity check on that component.

Invalid.simple: The hit effect appears at the reported contact point.
Invalid.technical: Declared as the uint8 slot 255 in the enum header. BuildHitEffectSpawnParams has no explicit Invalid case, so the default branch copies Request.Location into OutParams.Location.

notes: BuildHitEffectSpawnParams uses this value only for OutParams.Location. The effect asset comes from the damage row effect ids.
The implementation asks for the bone named waist. A nearby header comment records spine_03, so that discrepancy remains unresolved.
The Receiver fallback covers both a missing mesh component and a mesh without the requested bone.
The HitComponent branch dereferences Request.HitComponent without a validity check in the traced source.
